about: Ad Shield's own scriptlet rules (MIT). Each rule: hosts (each covers its subdomains) and scriptlets ([name, ...string args]) from src/scriptlets/lib.js. Built into build/scriptlets-main.js by tools/build.py; shipped in the package, never downloaded. Object paths and URL patterns: docs/research-v2.md section B. The YouTube anti-adblock dialog is closed by youtube-enforcement-dismiss, not hidden by CSS (hiding kept its scroll lock and pauses).

rules.about: Ad data removed before the player sees it, with as few hooks as possible (docs/DESIGN-v2.md, YouTube): the page-embedded player response and initial data (one-time setter traps; feed, search and Shorts ad items are pruned only here, later feed pages are left to rules/cosmetic/youtube.css), the player ad keys and a top-level Shorts entries list's isAd items in every JSON.parse / Response.json (plain key lookups after an indexOf needle check), and the youtubei player, get_watch, playlist, resolve_url and Shorts sequence fetch / XHR responses (player keys, also under resolve_url's endpoint.watchEndpoint.unserializedPrefetchData.playerResponse, and the Shorts isAd entries). Plus the 17 s "fake buffering" wait of flagged accounts (a native-code callback scheduled with setTimeout 17000) cut to 17 ms (research B section 1). No Promise.prototype.then or Function.prototype.toString hook and no ytcfg flag changes (uBO dropped onAbnormalityDetected and web_streaming_watch).

rules.about: m.youtube.com only (as uBO and AdGuard): ad items (adSlotRenderer) removed from the itemSectionRenderer.contents lists of the youtubei get_watch fetch response, the watch page's list below the player. The body is parsed only when it contains the word adSlotRenderer.

Fallbacks: for ads that still play (e.g. server-side inserted) mute, jump to the end of the ad, click Skip, unmute afterwards (research B recipe 11); and close YouTube's anti-adblock dialog properly (close() releases its scroll lock and backdrop) and resume a video it paused without the viewer while it is open or just closed (B.3); no repeated seeks within one ad and none in ads over 90 s (stitched streams); pauses from media keys, headphones or picture-in-picture (media session actions) are left alone.
